title: The listing tells you almost nothing
insight: The 2027 London listing carries only programme-wide and division-wide wording: no duties, team, language, deadline or salary [@R1-S02]. On 14 November 2026 it was no longer among the 194 live campus listings, while Frankfurt, Paris, Dubai, Doha and Tokyo CSG listings were [@R1-S03].
why_most_miss_it: Candidates quote the listing as if it described the job; it describes the firm.
use_it: Build your picture of the work from experienced-hire advertisements and say so. Ask: 'The listing is general by design. What does a summer analyst on your team produce in a typical week?'

title: Goldman's own definition of CSG
insight: Goldman describes the Client Solutions Group as the team that develops client relationships and delivers investment solutions for institutional and third-party wealth clients worldwide, across public and private asset classes [@R1-S10]. Its campus titles pair the name with 'Sales' [@R1-S04].
why_most_miss_it: People explain CSG from hearsay when a one-sentence official description exists.
use_it: Open 'what does CSG do?' with Goldman's two client types (institutional and third-party wealth) and two asset worlds (public and private), then add what you understand the junior work to be.

title: The real junior task list is public
insight: A London CSG sales-support advertisement lists the work: prepare and follow up client and prospect meetings, answer day-to-day client queries, work with product specialists, marketing, compliance and operations, and support the country head with market-intelligence and business-development presentations [@R1-S01].
why_most_miss_it: 'I'd support the team' is vague; the actual tasks are written down.
use_it: When asked what you would do as an analyst, name these tasks and connect one to a client outcome, for example a meeting note that makes sure every promise from the last meeting is kept.

title: CSG has its own strategy and data team
insight: The Global Client Solutions Group has a management and strategy team that runs sales budgeting, fundraising projections, weekly business summaries and Salesforce data governance [@R1-S13][@R1-S14].
why_most_miss_it: Coverage is imagined as conversations only; it is also a measured pipeline.
use_it: Show you understand that call notes and pipeline entries are how a relationship becomes the firm's knowledge. Ask how the team keeps its client records useful.

title: It is a matrix, mostly outside London
insight: Job advertisements show country teams crossed with channel: Germany and Austria from Frankfurt in German, France from Paris in French, Benelux needing native Dutch even when the seat is in London [@R1-S05][@R1-S06][@R1-S01].
why_most_miss_it: A London intern's list of teams looks complete because it lists what is visible from London.
use_it: Describe the structure as geography by client segment by function, and say which parts you know from published advertisements and which from one person's account.

title: Consultant Relations is a named team
insight: Goldman describes Consultant Relations as the team that works with the investment consultants who advise institutional investors; it works with regional institutional sales teams and builds a pipeline for them [@R1-S21].
why_most_miss_it: The consultant is treated as background when it is often the gatekeeper.
use_it: In any institutional answer, name the consultant's role: rating the strategy, running the tender, advising the trustees.

title: Distribution channels, in Goldman's words
insight: One Goldman advertisement lists the distribution channels as third party wealth, institutional, consultant, insurance and retirement [@R4-S09].
why_most_miss_it: Candidates divide the world into 'institutional and retail'.
use_it: Use the five-channel list to show you know insurance and retirement are treated as channels in their own right.

title: The UK endgame question has changed
insight: UK defined benefit schemes had an aggregate funding ratio of 133.7% and a £275.4bn surplus on the PPF measure at end October 2026 [@R3-S29], and the Pension Schemes Act 2026 makes surplus release easier, with regulations expected in 2027 [@R3-S20].
why_most_miss_it: Preparation written a few years ago still talks about deficits and repair plans.
use_it: Frame UK DB conversations as a choice between insuring the scheme and running it on. A good client question: 'Has the surplus changed how your trustees and sponsor think about buyout versus run-on?'

title: Rates just moved the other way
insight: Bank Rate was raised to 4% on 5 November 2026, the first increase since August 2023, with the 10-year gilt near 5.15% [@R3-S31].
why_most_miss_it: Anyone working from drafts written earlier in 2026 is still assuming cuts.
use_it: State the date and the direction, then the consequence you are sure of: liability values and hedging collateral move with gilt yields, so pension clients are affected directly.

title: The buyer is consolidating
insight: LGPS pools fell from eight to six in 2026 and funds must now delegate implementation to their pool [@R3-S21]; defined contribution defaults must reach £25bn by 2030 under the 2026 Act [@R3-S20].
why_most_miss_it: People list client types without noticing there are fewer, larger decision-makers each year.
use_it: Say what follows for coverage: fewer relationships, each worth more, each with a professional investment team that expects institutional-quality answers.

title: Kipling's title tells you the structure
insight: Goldman's September 2025 announcement titles Chloe Kipling 'co-head of EMEA Institutional Client Coverage'; she was previously head of the UK and Ireland institutional business [@R6-S02][@R6-S05]. Who leads UK institutional coverage now is not publicly established.
why_most_miss_it: Candidates guess at names or use an old title.
use_it: Use the exact title with its date if you mention her, and do not name a UK head. It is reasonable to ask how UK coverage fits within the EMEA institutional business.

title: OCIO is global and sits in an investing group
insight: Goldman reported $480bn of OCIO assets at 31 March 2026 [@R3-S09], and its OCIO teams sit within Multi-Asset Solutions, an investing group, working alongside sales and relationship professionals [@R1-S15][@R6-S11].
why_most_miss_it: The starting account placed OCIO as a third UK sales team.
use_it: Describe OCIO as an investment business that coverage teams work with. Ask: 'How do UK institutional coverage and the fiduciary management team divide a prospect between them?'

title: How the BAE mandate was actually won
insight: The BAE Systems trustees ran a competitive tender, advised by Redington, with Travers Smith as lawyers and PwC advising the sponsor; the schemes' in-house team moved to Goldman [@R3-S02]. In the year to March 2026 the trustee had Gallagher as a separate investment adviser overseeing the arrangement [@R7-S06].
why_most_miss_it: People cite the £23bn and stop.
use_it: Use it to show how a large mandate is decided: tender, adviser, lawyers, sponsor, then continuing independent oversight. Trust did not replace process.

title: Team transfer is the exception
insight: In-house teams moved in the largest deals (BAE Systems, UPS with 22 people) [@R7-S21], but nothing of the kind is reported for Short Brothers (£1.6bn) or Calor (£240m), which were ordinary tendered appointments [@R7-S15][@R7-S16].
why_most_miss_it: The starting account generalised from the most famous deal.
use_it: Say 'in some of the largest mandates the client's team has joined', never 'OCIO means absorbing the team'.

title: Two awards fit, and one loss
insight: Goldman won the fiduciary management / OCIO category at the European Pensions Awards (2 July 2026) and the Irish Pensions Awards (4 November 2026) [@R3-S10][@R3-S11]. It did not win Fiduciary Manager of the Year at the 2026 UK Pensions Awards, which went to Van Lanschot Kempen [@R3-S14].
why_most_miss_it: Naming 'the OCIO award' as a single known fact.
use_it: If awards come up, name the body and date, and add that an award shows a judging panel's view of a submission. It is not evidence of client outcomes.

title: Goldman's own account of why big schemes outsource
insight: A Goldman executive said in November 2025 that OCIO has moved from small schemes to large ones with in-house teams, because sponsors question whether running pensions is core business, maturing schemes shift to cashflow and hedging strategies, and chief investment officers are hard to replace [@R3-S07].
why_most_miss_it: Explaining OCIO only as 'small schemes lack resources'.
use_it: Give the three drivers and note they are the provider's view; a trustee might add cost and governance time.

title: The filings show OCIO is a low-rate scale business
insight: In 2025 advisory and OCIO alternative accounts averaged $112bn and earned 17 basis points, against 77 on funds and discretionary accounts [@R2-S01]. Goldman discloses no standalone OCIO revenue or fee.
why_most_miss_it: Assuming a huge mandate means a huge fee rate.
use_it: Explain that an OCIO provider is paid a low rate on a large base for delegated responsibility, and that the actual fee on any mandate is not public.

title: Third Party Wealth is the official name
insight: A Goldman press release of 28 April 2025 names an 'EMEA Third Party Wealth Business' [@R4-S01]; in the filings the same channel is 'Third-party distributed', $714bn at 30 September 2026 [@R2-S02].
why_most_miss_it: Mixing up team name and reporting line, or calling it 'retail'.
use_it: Use 'Third Party Wealth' for the team and 'third-party distributed' for the reported channel.

title: The EMEA head left in April 2026
insight: Hilary Lopez, head of the EMEA third party wealth business since 2021, was reported on 21 April 2026 to be leaving for a competitor, and no successor had been publicly named by the cutoff [@R6-S06]. Global co-heads Bryon Lake and Padideh Raphael were named that month [@R6-S08].
why_most_miss_it: Quoting a leader from an old article.
use_it: Do not name an EMEA head. If leadership comes up, refer to the global co-heads with the April 2026 date.

title: Who the UK team sells to
insight: Goldman's UK Third Party Wealth sales team is 'responsible for new business development' with private banks, wealth managers, financial advisers and multi-managers [@R1-S17], and that advertisement asked for a native English speaker and no other language.
why_most_miss_it: Thinking the end investor is the client.
use_it: Describe the chain: Goldman sells to a professional buyer who decides for many end clients. Being approved is permission to buy; assets come adviser by adviser.

title: The product push is wrappers and private markets
insight: Goldman launched 13 active ETFs in Europe in 2025 [@R4-S17] and in March 2026 its first evergreen fund under the revised ELTIF rules, within a G-Series of evergreen private-markets funds [@R4-S20]. No Goldman UK Long-Term Asset Fund or UK model portfolio service was found.
why_most_miss_it: Assuming the wealth team sells the same funds as ten years ago.
use_it: Ask how the UK team's conversations change when the product is an active ETF or a semi-liquid private-markets fund, and what suitability questions that raises.

title: Private Wealth as a buyer is only partly supported
insight: Goldman Private Wealth Management publicly describes an open-architecture alternatives platform that includes external managers [@R4-S27]. The specific examples in the starting account are not publicly established.
why_most_miss_it: Repeating a named example as fact.
use_it: Say 'Goldman's private wealth business uses external managers on its alternatives platform' and leave it there.

title: A product business with global leadership
insight: Liquidity Solutions has global heads, not regional ones, and serves financial institutions, hedge funds, institutions, corporates and wealth managers [@R5-S01][@R5-S04]. No public evidence supports a French-language requirement [@R5-S09].
why_most_miss_it: Treating it as another regional sales team.
use_it: Explain the client's problem: cash they may need tomorrow, where safety and access matter more than yield.

title: The rules for sterling money funds are being rewritten
insight: The FCA said on 8 June 2026 that the Government expects to repeal the UK Money Market Funds Regulation by end-2026, with new liquidity guidance of 40% weekly liquid assets for stable-value funds [@R5-S32]. Around 90% of sterling fund assets sit in EU-domiciled funds sold under temporary permissions [@R5-S34].
why_most_miss_it: Not knowing that the funds UK treasurers use are mostly domiciled abroad.
use_it: A client question: 'How are you thinking about the UK rule changes and the equivalence decision for your sterling liquidity funds?'

title: Cash left while long-term money arrived
insight: In Q3 2026 liquidity products had net outflows of $14bn while long-term assets took in $97bn [@R2-S02].
why_most_miss_it: Assuming all assets move together.
use_it: Use it to explain that liquidity balances follow clients' cash needs and rate expectations, so the measure that matters is average balance.

title: Insurance is a global vertical
insight: Goldman manages $651bn of insurers' general-account assets [@R5-S02] and offers partial to full outsourcing plus advice on asset-liability management and capital-efficient strategies [@R5-S02]. Advertisements show London and Frankfurt seats.
why_most_miss_it: Filing insurance under 'institutional' with pensions.
use_it: Explain the difference: an insurer is constrained by regulatory capital and accounting, so the same bond can be attractive to a pension fund and expensive for an insurer.

title: What 434 insurance investment heads said
insight: Goldman's 15th annual insurance survey (25 March 2026) polled 434 chief investment and finance officers; 62% plan to raise private-asset allocations, with asset-backed finance showing the highest net intended increase [@R5-S03].
why_most_miss_it: Not knowing Goldman publishes its clients' intentions every year.
use_it: Cite the survey as Goldman's own evidence of client demand, then add the limit: stated intentions are not allocations.

title: Two rule changes with dates
insight: Amended EU Solvency II rules apply from 30 January 2027 [@R5-S39]; in the UK the regulator consulted on letting insurers add assets to matching-adjustment portfolios before approval, within limits [@R5-S38].
why_most_miss_it: Speaking about 'Solvency II' as static.
use_it: Ask an insurance-facing interviewer which rule change is doing most to alter clients' asset choices.

title: Offices opened faster than leadership settled
insight: Goldman opened a Kuwait office in October 2025 and a Riyadh regional headquarters in December 2025 [@R5-S28][@R5-S29][@R5-S30]. The head of the Middle East client business left in September 2025, a co-head had stepped down in late 2024, and the current head is not publicly established [@R6-S14][@R6-S15].
why_most_miss_it: Naming a regional head from an old article.
use_it: Talk about the client base and the office build-out. Do not name a head.

title: Sovereign deals are partnerships, read the verbs
insight: Mubadala signed a $1bn separately managed account for Asia Pacific private credit [@R5-S04]; PIF signed a non-binding memorandum with no amount [@R7-S26]; the Qatar Investment Authority 'will target' $25bn of commitments, which one headline reported as 'commits' [@R7-S28].
why_most_miss_it: Adding the headline numbers together.
use_it: Distinguish a funded account, a memorandum and a target. That distinction is itself commercial awareness.

title: London staff were part of the Middle East team
insight: The departing regional head's team was based in London, Riyadh, Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Doha [@R6-S14]. 2027 CSG listings for Dubai and Doha state no language requirement [@R1-S07][@R1-S08].
why_most_miss_it: Assuming Gulf coverage is done only from the Gulf, or that Arabic is required.
use_it: Say that no language requirement appears in the advertisements read, which is weaker than saying Arabic is not needed.

title: The Benelux advertisement is the best evidence of all
insight: A London-based Benelux Client Solutions Group role (October 2026) says the team 'is responsible for new business development and managing existing institutional client relationships' and requires native Dutch [@R1-S01].
why_most_miss_it: Believing the name CSG excludes relationship management.
use_it: Use this as your evidence that at least one London team does both under one name.

title: The Dutch system change is a live client problem
insight: Thirty Dutch funds holding about €542bn had moved to the new pension system by 31 March 2026, with a deadline of 1 January 2028 [@R5-S35]. Goldman's 2022 purchase of NN Investment Partners brought more than 900 staff and a Dutch fiduciary business [@R2-S15].
why_most_miss_it: Treating NN IP as old news.
use_it: Connect the two: the acquisition gave Goldman a Dutch client base at the moment those clients are restructuring.

title: Nordics merged its channels in 2020
insight: In May 2020 the Nordic team became one organisation selling all asset classes to all client types, from Stockholm, Copenhagen and London [@R5-S26].
why_most_miss_it: Assuming every region splits institutional from wealth.
use_it: A counter-example to 'most regional teams split the same way as the UK'.

title: Why Iberia is missing from a London list
insight: Goldman moved its Iberia distribution head and her London team to Madrid in June 2021 [@R6-S13].
why_most_miss_it: Concluding a market is not covered because nobody in London mentions it.
use_it: Shows that coverage moved closer to clients after Brexit; a fair question is which teams still cover the Continent from London.

title: Who runs the group, with dates
insight: Matt Gibson is publicly described as head of the Client Solutions Group, having moved from investment banking into the asset management client business in early 2023 [@R6-S19][@R6-S20]. Marc Nachmann is global head of Asset & Wealth Management [@R2-S05].
why_most_miss_it: Using names without dates, or not knowing them at all.
use_it: Know the names and the dates you saw them. Do not drop them into answers unprompted.

title: The fiduciary leadership is well documented
insight: Ed Francis joined in November 2021 to lead UK fiduciary management and was titled 'Head of International OCIO and UK Fiduciary Management Team' in September 2024 [@R6-S03][@R6-S04]; Carolyn Schuster-Woldan joined as a managing director in September 2025 [@R6-S01].
why_most_miss_it: Not noticing that senior hiring continued in 2025.
use_it: This is the only public staffing evidence on the 'over-hired' remark, and it points the other way.

title: Titles: Executive Director is Vice President
insight: Outside the US Goldman uses 'Executive Director' as the working title for the Vice President corporate title, and Partner is by invitation in a named class of 109 for 2026 [@R1-S10][@R1-S27].
why_most_miss_it: Treating VP, Executive Director and Partner as three consecutive rungs.
use_it: Use titles correctly when you describe who you met or who interviews you.

title: What Goldman officially says about the process
insight: A video interview of about 30 minutes, then a final round of two to five interviews with people you could work with; applications are assessed throughout the season and candidates 'may hear back regarding different roles at different times' [@R1-S23].
why_most_miss_it: Mistaking one former intern's experience for the current process.
use_it: Prepare for the published shape. Treat everything else (who watches the video, team allocation, format) as unconfirmed.

title: What recruiters say they weigh
insight: Goldman recruiters describe interviews as behavioural or situational and say they weigh 'attitude and aptitude' and the candidate's thought process over existing technical knowledge [@R1-S24].
why_most_miss_it: Over-preparing jargon and under-preparing reasoning.
use_it: Practise explaining how you reached a view, including what you are unsure of.

title: Team allocation by keywords is unverified
insight: How London applicants are allocated to a team is not published; the claim that video answers decide it comes from one person [@R1-S41]. In the 2026 cycle some London listings carried a sub-track in the title, such as 'UK Institutional Sales' [@R1-S31].
why_most_miss_it: Tailoring answers to a rumour.
use_it: Talk about the clients and work you actually find interesting. Check your own application portal for any sub-track wording.

title: 'About 30%' is the segment, not the business
insight: Asset & Wealth Management was 28.6% of 2025 net revenues; asset management alone was 11.6% and wealth management 17.0% [@R2-S01]. Nothing is disclosed for the Client Solutions Group.
why_most_miss_it: Repeating '30% of revenue is asset management'.
use_it: Give both numbers and the reason they differ.

title: A commitment is not revenue
insight: Of $438bn of alternatives commitments raised from 2020 to 2025, $105bn was in non-fee-earning assets, most of which earns fees only when drawn and invested [@R2-S01]. Goldman's policy states private fund fees are charged on invested or committed capital depending on the fund [@R2-S01].
why_most_miss_it: Counting fundraising totals as fee-paying assets.
use_it: When you discuss a fundraise, ask what the fee base is and when fees start.

title: Goldman says passive is pushing its fees down
insight: Goldman's risk factors state that passive strategies have affected pricing and that if clients keep moving to lower-fee products 'our average effective management fee will decline further' [@R2-S01].
why_most_miss_it: Describing fee pressure as something that happens to other firms.
use_it: Quote the firm's own risk factor, then explain why product mix (alternatives at 58bp against fixed income at 17bp) matters to the strategy.

title: The website and the filing disagree
insight: Goldman's UK institutional site shows '$3.7+ trillion' with a footnote dated 30 September 2026, while the quarterly filing gives $4,097bn at the same date [@R2-S07][@R2-S02].
why_most_miss_it: Quoting whichever number was seen first.
use_it: Use the filing figure and name the date. If challenged, say the website figure uses a different basis that is not explained.

title: Goldman's definition of the coverage group
insight: Goldman defines its Client Coverage Group as 'dedicated to retaining, expanding and supporting existing client relationships' through client service, operational support and risk management, 'partnering closely with the sales team' [@R1-S11]. How it sits relative to CSG in London is not published.
why_most_miss_it: Assuming a clean sales/relationship split with fixed labels.
use_it: Say the two functions exist and overlap, and that you would ask how this team divides them.

title: What the coverage role actually handles
insight: The official task list: main point of contact across portfolio management, trading, operations, legal and compliance; client queries; reporting; account openings, restructures and terminations; questionnaires and audit requests [@R1-S11].
why_most_miss_it: Calling relationship management 'keeping clients happy'.
use_it: Name two of these tasks when you explain why relationship work needs investment and operational knowledge.

title: Pay structures differ by channel
insight: In the US wealth channel a CSG 'regional consultant' is paid base salary plus quarterly commission [@R1-S12]. No credible public source gives London analyst pay for this business [@R1-S41].
why_most_miss_it: Building a view of role prestige on two unverified salary figures.
use_it: Do not discuss pay differences as a reason for preferring sales or relationship management.

title: Trust did not remove oversight at BAE
insight: After appointing Goldman, the BAE Systems trustee kept a separate investment adviser, and the scheme's 2026 statement records Goldman as OCIO with Gallagher advising the trustee [@R7-S06].
why_most_miss_it: Thinking a deep relationship means the client stops checking.
use_it: Use it to show that delegation and independent oversight coexist, and that a good manager expects to be monitored.

title: A fiduciary client fired Goldman
insight: Pensioenfonds Vervoer appointed Goldman as fiduciary manager in 2006 and terminated the then €7bn mandate in 2010, citing underperformance [@R7-S48].
why_most_miss_it: Presenting only wins.
use_it: Your example for 'when is a client right to leave?': delegated responsibility with outcomes below what was promised.

title: The law makes relationships insufficient
insight: UK trustees must invite at least three unconnected providers to tender before a fiduciary manager runs 20% or more of scheme assets [@R3-S24].
why_most_miss_it: Believing a strong relationship can win a large UK mandate on its own.
use_it: A relationship earns an invitation and a fair hearing. The tender decides.

title: Private credit worries are now official
insight: The Bank of England's July 2026 stability report says private credit remains vulnerable to tighter financing and that redemption requests were elevated in several retail funds, with some limiting withdrawals [@R8-S52]. In the same period Goldman launched evergreen private-markets funds for wealth clients [@R4-S20].
why_most_miss_it: Presenting private markets for wealth as pure opportunity.
use_it: Hold both: demand is real and so is the liquidity mismatch. A fair question is how the firm explains redemption limits to an intermediary before the sale.

title: Consultants are consolidating too
insight: Mercer completed its acquisition of Cardano, and other consultancies have been bought by broking groups [@R8-S10][@R3-S34].
why_most_miss_it: Tracking asset managers' mergers and ignoring the gatekeepers'.
use_it: Fewer consultant research teams means each rating matters more, which raises the stakes for consultant relations.

title: BlackRock is the like-for-like OCIO rival
insight: BlackRock states over $400bn of OCIO and fiduciary assets at 31 March 2026 and won the £8bn British Coal Staff Superannuation Scheme mandate on 1 July 2026 after a competitive selection [@R8-S26]. It also holds Shell's Dutch fund, which was not part of Goldman's Shell mandate [@R7-S09].
why_most_miss_it: Comparing Goldman only with consultant-led fiduciary managers.
use_it: When asked 'why Goldman, not a competitor?', acknowledge that BlackRock offers a similar global model and argue from specifics, not from scale.

title: Check the names before you use them
insight: Nuveen completed its acquisition of Schroders in early October 2026 [@R8-S08]; State Street's manager has been State Street Investment Management since June 2025 [@R8-S05]; Columbia Threadneedle has left UK fiduciary management [@R8-S10].
why_most_miss_it: Using last year's competitor names.
use_it: Getting names and ownership right is a cheap, visible sign of current knowledge.

title: Goldman's manager-selection arm is a real differentiator, with a catch
insight: Goldman's External Investing Group has more than $528bn across traditional and alternative strategies and relationships with over 1,000 private equity managers [@R8-S19]. That supports the open-architecture claim; it also means a client must ask how the firm chooses between its own funds and external ones.
why_most_miss_it: Saying 'global platform' with nothing behind it.
use_it: Name the capability, the number and the conflict question in one answer.

title: AI is already doing the first draft
insight: 81% of institutional sales and service teams use AI to generate and refine RFP content and 77% for meeting notes; far fewer use it to identify prospects (26%) or plan strategy (26%) [@R8-S41]. Isio found 85% of fiduciary managers use AI for lower-risk tasks such as drafting [@R8-S10].
why_most_miss_it: Either 'AI will replace sales' or 'relationships are irreplaceable'.
use_it: Answer at task level: drafting is automated, checking and judgement are not, and a junior's value moves towards verifying and understanding what the draft says.

title: What is established about Goldman's AI rules
insight: Secondary reports of a Bloomberg article (2 November 2026) say October guidance limited AI coding tools to engineers [@R2-S08]. Goldman's own assistant was rolled out firmwide in June 2025 with a version for asset and wealth management staff [@R2-S13].
why_most_miss_it: Saying 'Goldman banned Claude'.
use_it: If AI comes up, describe supervised use for drafting and analysis, and say you would follow the firm's policy on which tools are permitted.

title: No evidence yet on junior hiring
insight: No credible source found quantifies cuts to entry-level client-facing hiring in asset management because of AI [@R8-S41].
why_most_miss_it: Asserting a trend because it sounds plausible.
use_it: Say what is observed (tasks changing) and what is not established (hiring effects).

title: Markets, not new money, drove 2025 growth
insight: More than 80% of asset managers' gross revenue growth in 2025 came from market appreciation, and costs have grown faster than revenues since 2010 [@R8-S38].
why_most_miss_it: Assuming distribution drives most growth.
use_it: Use it to argue why net new assets and retention matter more when markets stop helping. It is an industry estimate, so say so.

title: Admit what is not public
insight: Goldman does not disclose revenue, assets, flows, headcount or fee rates for the Client Solutions Group, any EMEA client team or the UK [@R2-S01].
why_most_miss_it: Inventing team-level numbers to sound informed.
use_it: Saying 'that is not published, but here is what the firm-wide figures suggest' is stronger than a confident guess.

title: Ask about the split, do not assert it
insight: Published evidence shows a 'Client Solutions Group' doing both new business and existing relationships in one London team [@R1-S01] and a 'Client Coverage Group' defined around existing relationships [@R1-S11].
why_most_miss_it: Telling the interviewer how their team is organised.
use_it: A strong closing question: 'On your team, where does a new mandate pass from the person who won it to the person who looks after it?'
